newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks rally to 11th record close of 1997.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks rally to 11th record close of 1997.

text.p: CHANGE CHANGE
NIKKEI 18198.74 +157.41 LME CASH NICKEL US$8070 +75.0
CANDLR 1.3692 LME CASH ALUM US$1638.0 -29.0
CAN 30-YR 111.20 +0.75 APR BRENT CRUDE US$19.80 +0.16
* Toronto stocks soared to their 11th record close of 1997 on Friday * TSE also hit an intraday high of 6277.42 * Bank rally continues, transports up 2 pct * 107 million shares traded
Toronto stocks soared to new heights on Friday as Canada's big banks pushed higher and markets shrugged off a jump in U.S. non-farm payrolls.
The TSE 300 Composite Index jumped 53.66 points to close at 6268.39, its 11th record close of 1997. The previous record was set on February 19.
The key index set an all-time high of 6277.42 earlier in the session. Trading was heavy with 107.9 million shares changing hands worth C$1.83 billion.
"We've finished the week in pretty grand style," said Fred Ketchen, director of equity trading for ScotiaMcLeod Inc.
U.S. nonfarm payrolls rose by 339,000 in February on Friday against a revised 247,000 increase in January. Economists had forecast a rise of 230,000 in February.
"In previous times if we had seen these non-farm payrolls numbers, the markets would have been on their knees. Today, it worked the opposite way," Ketchen said.
He said investors may still be focused on U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's comment this week that stock prices are not too high if profit estimates are correct.
"I think that has made people feel a whole lot more comfortable and it carried on today," Ketchen said.
On the TSE, gains in 12 of 14 sub-groups were led by financial services, transportation and base metals. They overwhelmed losses in precious metals and forestry.
--- HOT STOCKS ---
* Bank stocks continued to climb after a record first quarter for the Big Six banks. Bank of Montreal added 1.65 to close at 53.70 after hitting a 52-week high of 54.50.
Bank of Nova Scotia rose 1.40 to close at 55.70, off a year-high of 56.00 reached earlier in the session.
* Petro-Canada topped the most-active list, up 0.15 at 20.10 on 3.8 million shares.
